Next followed the Aslam tribe. They comprised of four hundred soldiers and bore two flags. One was carried by Hadhrat Buraydah bin Husayb (RA) while Hadhrat Naajiya bin A'jam (RA) carried the other. They also called out "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they, O Abul Fadhl?" "That is the tribe of Aslam," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "What have I to do with the Aslam tribe?" responded Abu Sufyaan, "There has never been any dispute between us." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said to him, "They are a nation who have entered the fold of Islaam."
Thereafter, five hundred men belonging to the Banu Ka'b bin Amr tribe passed by with Hadhrat Bishr bin Shaybaan (RA) carrying their flag. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "They are the Ka'b bin Amr tribe," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "O yes," acknowledged Abu Sufyaan, "they are the allies of Muhammad ﷺ." They also procalimed "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan.
The Muzayna tribe passed next. They were a thousand strong who included a hundred horsemen and they carried three flags. Their flag bearers were Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Muqarrin, Hadhrat Bilaal bin Haarith and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA). They also cried "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "That is the Muzayna tribe," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). "What have I to do with the Muzayna tribe?" responded Abu Sufyaan, "They have also come to me from the peaks of their mountains with their weapons clattering."
The Juhayna tribe passed next with their leader. They consisted of eight hundred soldiers and bore four flags. There was a flag with Hadhrat Abu Zur'ah Ma'bad bin Khaalid (RA), another with Hadhrat Suwayd bin Sakhr, a third with Hadhrat Raafi bin Makeeth (RA) and the fourth with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Badr (RA). They also cried "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan.
Thereafter, came the Kinaana tribe that consisted of the Banu Layth, the Banu Dhamra and Banu Sa'd bin Bakr families. They numbered two hundred and Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Laythi (RA) bore their flag. They also cried "Allaahu Akbar!" thrice as they passed Abu Sufyaan. Abu Sufyaan asked, "Who are they?" "That is Banu Bakr tribe," replied Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). Abu Sufyaan said, "Oh yes! By Allaah! They are a tribe of misfortune. It is because of them that Muhammad ﷺ is attacking us. [^1] Swear by Allaah that they (the Quraysh) did not consult with me and I had no knowledge of the matter. When the news of what happened reached me, I was most disgusted. Nevertheless, the matter was predestined." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) said to Abu Sufyaan, "Allaah has destined good in this offensive of Rasulullaah ﷺ against you as you all enter the fold of Islaam."

After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, the Banu Bakr tribe struck up an allegiance with the Quraysh while the Banu Khuzaa'ah aligned with the Muslims. However, a joint attack on the Banu Khuzaa'ah by the Banu Bakr and the Quraysh led to the annulment of the Treaty, allowing the Muslims the opportunity to march on to Makkah. Abu Sufyaan was referring to this incident.
